headline: High risk of prompt/data leakage and cascading errors from shared file-backed research outputs into a writable orchestration graph.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; LangGraph can wire developer-defined tools and has no self-isolation. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge would let attacker-controlled research content influence downstream instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but not proven by the profiles alone, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, MCP server, or copied outputs are parsed as instructions
IF LangGraph nodes consume gpt-researcher text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A's raw outputs into B
Add a provenance tag and reject untrusted instruction-like text
Separate workspaces per agent
Require human review before any tool-using node executes
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and provenance-aware parsers

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, images, and secrets, while LangGraph can write application-defined files and uses broad network egress via developer tools. If they share a workspace or checkpointer, sensitive research artifacts can flow into B and then out through model/provider calls. The default pairwise blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, checkpointer, or mounted volume
IF B's nodes send shared state to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Use separate storage roots for each agent
Exclude secrets and local documents from shared state
Rotate any API keys exposed to A
Restrict B's tool nodes to non-sensitive state
requires-engineering: encrypt and partition the checkpointer store

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access; LangGraph additionally writes files and can orchestrate subprocesses, while gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses and read files. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to shared artifacts are plausible. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, cache, or checkpointer namespace
IF concurrent runs target the same research project state
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on the same project
Use per-run namespaces in the checkpointer
requires-engineering: add transactional state updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that produces reports and citations, and LangGraph is a graph orchestrator that can route those outputs into downstream nodes. If B treats A's text as authoritative, errors or fabricated citations can cascade into actions or published outputs. Because the pair can default to this handoff, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF B routes A's report into action-taking or publishing nodes without verification
IF A's citations are consumed as facts by downstream nodes
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action
Require source-link checks for every citation
Mark A's output as untrusted in graph state
Limit downstream nodes to read-only review
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against sources

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets, while LangGraph's state is application-defined and may persist in a checkpointer store. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into shared state, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR boundaries, so medium reflects a plausible compliance mismatch rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in LangGraph checkpointer state
IF retention or deletion requests must propagate from A's documents to B's persisted graph state
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the checkpointer
Document retention for shared state
Purge per-run state after completion
Map data classes to allowed storage locations
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export propagation
